full_judgment:
The judgments and decrees, which are called in question in the instant writ petitions, are narrated in the table below for ready reference:- 

 S.L. Nos.	Writ Petition Nos.	Judgment and decree dated	Land Survey Tribunal Case Nos.	Land Survey Tribunals (LST) concerned 

 All these writ petitions arise out of judgment and decrees passed by the land survey tribunals and all arise out of suits filed in land survey Tribunals. When the matters were taken up for hearing our attention was drawn to some judgments passed by other Benches of this division involving similar matters and issues arising out of judgment and decrees or judgment and orders passed by the Land Survey Tribunal. For our convenience we have particularly perused the judgment tiled in writ petition No. 11463 of 2016 and another in writ petition No. 515 of 2017 inter alia another decision. In these writ petitions Rule were disposed of primarily on the ground of writ not being maintainable pursuant to enactment of Section 145 B of the S.A.T Act. 

 Section 145 B provides for setting up Laud Survey Appellate Tribunal. The objective of enacting section 145 B is that any person aggrieved by any judgment and decree or order passed by any land survey tribunal may file an appeal before the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal. The Overall view taken in these judgments while disposing of these writ petitions are that judgment and decrees and orders passed by the Tribunal involving question of law and fart needs reassessment of evidence and other factors which is not possible or permissible in writ and therefore writ is not maintainable. 

 We have also perused the writ petition before us which involves similar question and issues of law and fact. For sake of convenience we are inclined to take up writ petition No. 4259 of 2022 which arises out of a judgment and decree in which Rule was issued in the following terms: 

 "Let a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondent No. 5 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2022 (decree sinned on 31.01.2022) passed by the learned Judge of the Land Survey Tribunal, Barishal decreeing the suit of the plaintiff in Land Survey Tribunal Case No. 983 of 2013 (Annexure-A) to the writ petition should not be declared illegal, improper, unjust, erroneous, without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper." 

 Upon perusal of the writ petition it also appears that the judgment and decree passed by the tribunal inherently and primarily involve question of facts and evidences which need reassessment inter aria other relevant procedures. Drawing support from the judgment in writ petition No. 11463 of 2016 and writ petition No. 515 of 2017 including some other judgments with which we are in respectful agreement with, we are of the considered view upon examination and scrutiny of all the writ petitions before us that these judgments involves question of law and fact which call for reassessment of evidences including exhausting other procedures which is not possible in writ jurisdiction.
